mainTopic: The rebuilding of the משמרות, the reason the מעמדות read מעשה בראשית, their weekly fasts, and how two people can share the five-verse reading of בראשית
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא. The four priestly families that returned from exile were split by lottery into twenty-four משמרות, and ידעיה kept first place even over יהויריב. The גמרא then asks why the ordinary Jews of each משמר read מעשה בראשית. רב אסי answers that the world stands in the merit of the מעמדות and the קרבנות, and that when there is no בית המקדש, reading the סדר קרבנות counts as bringing them. A ברייתא describes the אנשי מעמד fasting Monday through Thursday, each day for a need linked to that day of creation, with no fast on Friday or שבת. Three אמוראים explain why there was no fast on Sunday: רבי יוחנן, רבי שמואל בר נחמני, and ריש לקיש with his teaching about the נשמה יתירה. Next the גמרא asks how two people can share the five verses of בראשית. רב says the second reader repeats a verse (דולג), and שמואל says the middle verse is split (פוסק), and the reasoning behind each view is explained. A ברייתא then seems to challenge both views. The גמרא begins to answer that its case is different, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Four families are divided into twenty-four watches by lottery
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. The נביאים divided the four returning priestly families into twenty-four משמרות by drawing lots. Each of the four families drew six lots.
steps.simpleTranslation: They divided them and set them up as twenty-four watches. They mixed up the lots and put them in a box. ידעיה came and drew his own portion plus his fellows' portions, six in all. חרים came and drew his own portion plus his fellows' portions, six in all. פשחור did the same, and so did אמר.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא, which began on the previous amud, finishes describing how the full system of twenty-four משמרות was rebuilt from only four families that came back from exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Originally there were twenty-four priestly families. Only four returned, so each of the four was split into six groups to fill all twenty-four slots. A lottery decided which of the old twenty-four names each group would carry.

keyTerms.meaning: a box or urn for drawing lots
the portion of his fellows (the other lots)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think only four watches served after the exile. Four families were split into six groups each, so the full twenty-four משמרות were restored.

phrases.english: and they divided them and established them as twenty-four,
they mixed them and put them in a lottery box.
phrases.notes: The names of the twenty-four watches were written on lots.

phrases.english: Jedaiah came and took his portion
and the portion of his fellows: six,
phrases.notes: His own lot plus five more.

phrases.english: Harim came and took his portion
and the portion of his fellows: six,
and likewise Pashhur, and likewise Immer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא begun on the previous amud about the four families that returned from exile.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The four returning families were split by lottery into twenty-four משמרות, six per family.

steps.title: Jedaiah keeps first place even if Jehoiarib returns
steps.stepSummary: The נביאים set a condition. Even if יהויריב, the original first watch, comes back, ידעיה stays first and יהויריב comes after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The prophets among them also made a condition: even if יהויריב, who used to be the head watch, comes up, ידעיה will not be pushed out of its place. Rather, ידעיה is the main one, and יהויריב is secondary to it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds one more rule from the נביאים about the order of the new משמרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the old system יהויריב was the first watch. Since ידעיה returned and helped rebuild the system, the נביאים protected its new first place against any later return of יהויריב. This finishes the ברייתא's account.

keyTerms.meaning: head of the watches (first in order)

steps.whatToRemember: After the exile, the משמרות were rebuilt from four families. ידעיה became first and keeps that place permanently, even over the original first family, יהויריב.

phrases.english: And likewise the prophets among them stipulated:
that even if Jehoiarib, head of the watches, comes up,
phrases.notes: Comes up to ארץ ישראל from exile.

phrases.english: Jedaiah will not be pushed out of its place.
Rather, Jedaiah is primary,
and Jehoiarib is secondary to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a final condition to the reorganization described in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ידעיה holds permanent priority over יהויריב in the order of the משמרות.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the watch reads the Creation story?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the ordinary Jews of each משמר gather in their towns and read מעשה בראשית. It then asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'The Israelites of that watch gather in their towns and read the story of Creation.' Where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the topic of the משמרות and returns to a new line of the משנה. It asks for a source, which sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the non-כהנים of the watch read מעשה בראשית but gives no reason. The question מנהני מילי asks for a basis for this practice and opens a new section.

keyTerms.meaning: the watch on duty that week
the story of Creation (start of בראשית)
from where do we know these things?

phrases.english: And the Israelites of that watch
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה.

phrases.english: gather in their towns
and read the act of Creation.
From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic by quoting the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or reason that the Israelites of the watch read מעשה בראשית.

steps.title: Heaven and earth exist because of the watches
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי teaches that without the מעמדות, heaven and earth would not continue to exist. He brings a verse in which אברהם asks God how he will know he will inherit the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יעקב בר אחא said in the name of רב אסי: If not for the מעמדות, heaven and earth would not continue to exist. As it says: 'And he said, Lord God, by what shall I know that I will inherit it?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer the question. It says the whole world depends on the מעמדות, and it starts to bring a verse as support.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim connects the מעמדות to the survival of creation itself. That hints at why the people of the watch read the story of Creation. The verse is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: non-priestly groups linked to the Temple service

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main idea: the קרבנות, and the מעמדות connected to them, keep the world standing. That explains why the people of the watch read about Creation.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov bar Aha said that Rav Asi said:
Were it not for the non-priestly watches,
heaven and earth would not continue to exist,
as it is stated: 'And he said: Lord God,'
'by what shall I know that I shall inherit it?'
phrases.notes: בראשית טו:ח

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּר אַחָא אָמַר רַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The world exists in the merit of the מעמדות, as hinted in אברהם's question to God.

steps.title: Abraham asks whether his children will be wiped out for sinning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the verse. אברהם asked whether God would destroy Israel if they sin, as He did to דור המבול and דור הפלגה. God answered no.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said: Master of the World! What if Israel sins before You? Will You do to them what You did to the generation of the Flood and the generation of the Tower? God said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining what אברהם meant by his question in the verse. This sets up God's real answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אברהם was not doubting the promise itself. He was worried that his descendants' sins could lead to total destruction. God promises not to destroy them.

keyTerms.meaning: the generation of the Tower of Babel

phrases.english: Abraham said: Master of the Universe!
Perhaps Israel will sin before You,
will You do to them
as to the generation of the flood and the generation of the dispersion?
He said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the verse quoted in step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: God promised אברהם that Israel would not be destroyed for their sins, as earlier generations were.

steps.title: God points Abraham to the offerings
steps.stepSummary: אברהם asks how his descendants will keep the land. God answers by commanding him to take animals for offerings, which hints at the קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said before Him: Master of the World! Tell me, by what will I inherit it? God said to him: 'Take for Me a three-year-old heifer, and a three-year-old goat, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם asks what will protect his descendants, and God's answer points to קרבנות. This explains how the verse connects to the מעמדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals listed are the kinds later brought as קרבנות. The message is that the merit of the offerings protects Israel and, through them, the world. The מעמדות are part of that offering service, which ties back to רב אסי's claim. Step 8 completes the link to reading מעשה בראשית.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base of the idea that קרבנות, and their replacement through learning about them, keep the world in existence.

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the Universe!
Tell me, with what shall I inherit it?
He said to him: 'Take for Me a three-year-old heifer'
'and a three-year-old goat, etc.'
phrases.notes: בראשית טו:ט

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם! הוֹדִיעֵנִי בַּמֶּה אִירָשֶׁנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After God promises not to destroy Israel, אברהם asks what will protect them, and God answers.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The merit of the קרבנות is how Israel will keep the land and how the world is preserved.

steps.title: Abraham asks what happens when there is no Temple
steps.stepSummary: אברהם accepts that the קרבנות will protect his descendants. But he asks what will protect them once the בית המקדש is destroyed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אברהם said before God: Master of the World! That works well while the בית המקדש is standing. But when the בית המקדש is not standing, what will happen to them?
steps.whatsHappening: אברהם asks a follow-up question. If the קרבנות are what protect the Jewish people, what will protect them when there is no בית המקדש to bring קרבנות in?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 6, God's answer was the קרבנות. That answer only works while the בית המקדש exists. Here אברהם points out this gap and asks about the time of גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World, a way of speaking to God
It works out well (that part makes sense)

phrases.english: He said before Him: Master of the World!
This works out well at a time when the Temple is standing.
At a time when the Temple is not standing,
what will become of them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question on God's answer in Step 6, that the קרבנות will protect Israel.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What will protect Israel when there is no בית המקדש and no קרבנות?

steps.title: Reading the order of offerings counts as offering them
steps.stepSummary: God answers that He has already arranged the סדר קרבנות. When Jews read it, God treats it as if they brought the קרבנות, and He forgives their sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: God said to him: I already set up for them the order of קרבנות. When they read it before Me, I will count it as if they brought the קרבנות before Me, and I will forgive them for all their sins.
steps.whatsHappening: God answers אברהם. When the בית המקדש is gone, reading the קרבנות takes their place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answers the gap from Step 7. Reading about the קרבנות is treated as if the person actually brought them, and it brings the same forgiveness. This also explains the משנה from Step 3: the קרבנות keep the world existing, so the אנשי מעמד read about the creation of the world while the קרבנות are being brought.

keyTerms.meaning: The order of offerings (the sections of the Torah about the קרבנות)
I count it for them (I credit them)

steps.whatToRemember: When there is no בית המקדש, reading the קרבנות counts as if we brought them, and it brings forgiveness.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for the custom of saying the sections about the קרבנות in daily davening.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּבָר תִּקַּנְתִּי לָהֶם סֵדֶר קׇרְבָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: He said to him: I have already set up for them the order of offerings.
When they read them before Me,

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲלֶה אֲנִי עֲלֵיהֶם כְּאִילּוּ הִקְרִיבוּם לְפָנַי
phrases.english: I credit them as though they had offered them before Me,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנִי מוֹחֵל לָהֶם עַל כׇּל עֲוֹנוֹתֵיהֶם.
phrases.english: and I forgive them for all their sins.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אברהם's question from Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Reading the סדר קרבנות is treated as if the קרבנות were brought, and it brings forgiveness.

steps.title: The priests pray and the townspeople fast four days
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the אנשי משמר prayed that the קרבן would be accepted. Meanwhile, the אנשי מעמד gathered in the בית הכנסת and fasted Monday through Thursday.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: The members of the משמר would pray that their brothers' קרבן be accepted favorably. The members of the מעמד would gather in the בית הכנסת and keep four fasts: on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a ברייתא about what each group did during its week. It ends by listing the four fast days, which sets up the next step about the purpose of each day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא describes two groups. The אנשי משמר prayed for the קרבן to be accepted. The אנשי מעמד, the ordinary Jews of that week's group, gathered in the בית הכנסת and fasted four days. The purpose of each fast is given in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught (this opens a ברייתא)
The members of the משמר, the group serving that week
The ordinary Jews of that week's group, who stayed in their towns

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two groups. The אנשי משמר are the ones whose קרבן is being brought, and they pray. The אנשי מעמד are the ones who gather in the בית הכנסת and fast.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין
phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: the members of the priestly watch would pray
for the offering of their brothers, that it be accepted with favor.
And the members of the non-priestly group would gather in the synagogue,
and keep four fasts:
on Monday, on Tuesday, on Wednesday, and on Thursday.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַנְשֵׁי מִשְׁמָר הָיוּ מִתְפַּלְּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section that describes in more detail what the אנשי משמר and אנשי מעמד did.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אנשי משמר prayed for the קרבן to be accepted, and the אנשי מעמד fasted Monday through Thursday.

steps.title: What each fast day was for
steps.stepSummary: Each fast had its own purpose. Monday was for people at sea. Tuesday was for desert travelers. Wednesday was so the disease אסכרא would not strike children. Thursday was for pregnant and nursing women.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Monday they fasted for those traveling at sea. On Tuesday, for those traveling through deserts. On Wednesday, that the disease אסכרא should not strike the children. On Thursday, for pregnant and nursing women: that pregnant women should not miscarry, and that nursing women should be able to nurse their children.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and explains what the people prayed for on each of the four fast days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day matches what was created on that day of creation. The sea was created on Monday and dry land on Tuesday. The lights were created on Wednesday, and the word מאורות hints at מארות, curses. Living creatures were created on Thursday. This fits the משנה, where the אנשי מעמד read about the creation of the world.

keyTerms.meaning: Those who go down to the sea (sailors and sea travelers)
A dangerous throat disease (croup or diphtheria)

phrases.english: On Monday: for those who travel the sea.
On Tuesday: for those who travel through deserts.
On Wednesday: about croup,
that it should not strike the children.
On Thursday: for pregnant women and nursing women.
Pregnant women: that they should not miscarry.
Nursing women: that they should be able to nurse their children.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the purpose of each of the four fast days listed in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each fast day had its own purpose, matching what was created on that day.

steps.title: No fasting on Friday or Shabbat
steps.stepSummary: They did not fast on ערב שבת out of respect for שבת. Through a קל וחומר, they certainly did not fast on שבת itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: On ערב שבת they did not fast, out of respect for שבת. All the more so, they did not fast on שבת itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains why there was no fast on Friday or שבת. This leaves Sunday unexplained, which sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fasting on Friday would make a person enter שבת weak and hungry, and that does not honor שבת. If even the day before שבת is protected, then שבת itself certainly is.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so (a logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one)

phrases.english: And on Shabbat eve they would not fast,
because of the honor of Shabbat,
and all the more so on Shabbat itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and explains why Friday and שבת are not fast days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is no fasting on ערב שבת out of respect for שבת, and certainly none on שבת itself.

steps.title: Why no fast on Sunday?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explained why there was no fast on Friday and שבת. The גמרא now asks why there was no fast on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: On Sunday, what is the reason they did not fast?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the one day the ברייתא did not explain, Sunday. This sets up the three answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sunday has no שבת-related reason to skip fasting. So the גמרא wants to know why the fasts started only on Monday.

keyTerms.meaning: Sunday, the first day of the week

phrases.english: On Sunday, what is the reason they did not fast?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The ברייתא explained Friday and שבת, and this asks about the remaining day, Sunday.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why did the אנשי מעמד not fast on Sunday?

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: because of the Christians
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says they did not fast on Sunday because of the נוצרים, the Christians.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Because of the Christians.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the first answer to why there was no fast on Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sunday is the Christians' special day. If Jews made something special of that day, the Christians might claim that even the Jews treat their day as significant. So the fasts were not held on Sunday.

keyTerms.meaning: A major אמורא of ארץ ישראל

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: Because of the Christians.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question in Step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They avoided fasting on Sunday because of the Christians, for whom Sunday is a special day.

steps.title: רבי שמואל בר נחמני: the third day after man was created
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמואל בר נחמני gives a different reason. Sunday is the third day after man was created, and the third day is the weakest, so it is not a good day to fast.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמואל בר נחמני said: Because it is the third day from the creation of man.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a different answer to why there was no fast on Sunday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Man was created on Friday, so Sunday is the third day counting from then. The third day after a wound, such as a מילה, is known as the weakest and most painful day. So this day is treated as a time of weakness, and they did not add the burden of fasting.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are two reasons for not fasting on Sunday: רבי יוחנן says because of the Christians, and רבי שמואל בר נחמני says Sunday is the weak third day after man's creation. ריש לקיש gives a third reason in the next step.
steps.confusionAlert: Third does not mean the third day of the week. Count from Friday, when man was created: Friday, שבת, Sunday. Sunday is the third day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said:
Because it is the third day after the creation of man.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא שְׁלִישִׁי לַיְצִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, different answer to the question in Step 12, alongside רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Sunday is the third day after man's creation, a day of weakness, so they did not fast on it.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: no Sunday fast because the extra soul has just left
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ gives a third reason for not fasting on Sunday. A person receives a נשמה יתירה on ערב שבת, and it is taken away on מוצאי שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Because of the extra soul. As ריש לקיש said: An extra soul is given to a person on ערב שבת, and at the end of שבת they take it away from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still answering why they did not fast on Sunday. רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ offers a third answer, after רבי יוחנן and רבי שמואל בר נחמני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת a person has an extra soul, a נשמה יתירה. When it leaves after שבת, the person is left weaker than usual. So Sunday is a bad day to add the strain of a fast. Like רבי שמואל בר נחמני, he explains the rule through weakness, but the cause he gives is different.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra soul given to a person for שבת

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Because of the extra soul,
phrases.notes: This is his reason for not fasting on Sunday.

phrases.english: as Reish Lakish said:
phrases.notes: He brings his own teaching elsewhere as the background.

phrases.english: an extra soul is given to a person
on Shabbat eve,
and at the end of Shabbat they take it from him,

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מִפְּנֵי נְשָׁמָה יְתֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third answer to the question of step 12, alongside the answers of steps 13 and 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No fast on Sunday because a person is weakened after losing the נשמה יתירה on מוצאי שבת.

steps.title: The verse behind the extra soul: 'He rested and was refreshed'
steps.stepSummary: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ reads the word וינפש as 'וי נפש', meaning 'woe, the soul is lost'. This shows that a soul departs once שבת ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'He rested and was refreshed (וַיִּנָּפַשׁ).' Once he has rested, woe, the soul is lost!
steps.whatsHappening: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ brings a פסוק as the source for his idea of the extra soul.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word וַיִּנָּפַשׁ is split into two words: וַי (woe) and נֶפֶשׁ (soul). The phrase 'כיון ששבת', 'once שבת has passed', tells us when the soul leaves. This proves both that there is an extra soul and that it is lost after שבת.

phrases.english: As it is stated: "He rested and was refreshed."
Once he has rested (once Shabbat has passed),
woe, the soul is lost.
phrases.notes: This is a wordplay: וַיִּנָּפַשׁ is read as וַי נֶפֶשׁ.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source in the פסוק for the claim made in step 15.
steps.raayaObject: That a נשמה יתירה exists on שבת and leaves when שבת ends.
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות לא:יז, 'שבת וינפש', read as 'וי נפש'.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three reasons for not fasting on Sunday: the נוצרים (רבי יוחנן), the third day after man was created is the weakest (רבי שמואל בר נחמני), and the loss of the נשמה יתירה (רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ).

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: Sunday's readings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: on Sunday the אנשי מעמד read בראשית and יהי רקיע.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first day of the week, they read 'In the beginning' and 'Let there be a firmament'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. It quotes the משנה's line about Sunday's Torah reading so that it can discuss it next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day, the אנשי מעמד read the part of the creation story that matches that day. On Sunday they read the first two sections: day one (בראשית) and day two (יהי רקיע). This line is a setup for the questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: On the first day of the week (Sunday)
The section of day one of creation (בראשית א:א-ה)
The section of day two of creation (בראשית א:ו-ח)

phrases.english: On the first day (Sunday)
they read "In the beginning" and "Let there be a firmament."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic: the גמרא returns to the משנה's list of daily readings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On Sunday the readings are בראשית and יהי רקיע.

steps.title: ברייתא: two people read בראשית, one reads יהי רקיע
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the בראשית section is read by two people, while the יהי רקיע section is read by one.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: 'In the beginning' is read by two people, and 'Let there be a firmament' is read by one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells how many people read each section. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא adds a detail that the משנה did not say: who reads what. Two people share בראשית, and יהי רקיע gets a single reader. This detail is what creates the coming problem.

phrases.english: It was taught:
"In the beginning" is read by two people,
"Let there be a firmament" is read by one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the משנה's reading list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בראשית is read by two people; יהי רקיע is read by one.

steps.title: How can two people share only five verses?
steps.stepSummary: יהי רקיע has three verses, so one reader makes sense. But בראשית has only five verses, and each reader must read at least three. So how can two people read it?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that 'Let there be a firmament' is read by one, since it is three verses. But why is 'In the beginning' read by two? It is only five verses, and it was taught: One who reads from the Torah may not read fewer than three verses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. Two readers would need at least six verses, but בראשית has only five.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule from מסכת מגילה is that each reader must read at least three verses. Three verses for one reader works out exactly. Five verses split between two people means one of them reads fewer than three, which breaks that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (the next part is the problem)
One may not read fewer than three verses

steps.confusionAlert: The section of בראשית here means only day one of creation (בראשית א:א-ה), which is five verses. It does not mean the whole פרשה.

phrases.english: Granted, "Let there be a firmament" is read by one,
since it is three verses.
But why is "In the beginning" read by two?
It is only five verses,
and it was taught: One who reads from the Torah
may not read fewer than three verses!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ברייתא of step 18 using the three-verse minimum.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that two people read בראשית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Five verses cannot give two readers three verses each, which the rule from מגילה requires.

steps.title: רב: the second reader repeats a verse
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the second reader goes back and repeats a verse (דולג). That way each reader reads three verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: He repeats (a verse).
steps.whatsHappening: רב gives the first answer to the problem: one verse is read twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reader reads verses 1-3. The second reader starts again at verse 3 and goes through verse 5. Verse 3 is read by both, so each reader reaches three verses without cutting any verse.

keyTerms.meaning: Repeats (the second reader goes back over a verse already read)

steps.confusionAlert: Here דולג means 'repeats'. It does not mean 'skips ahead'.

phrases.english: Rav said: He repeats a verse.
phrases.notes: The second reader repeats the last verse the first reader read.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Five verses cannot cover two readers.
steps.terutzMaskana: Repeating verse 3 gives each reader three verses.

steps.title: שמואל: split the middle verse in half
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that the middle verse is split (פוסק). Each reader reads two and a half verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: He splits (a verse).
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer to the same problem: cut verse 3 into two halves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of repeating a verse, the third verse is divided. The first reader stops in the middle of it, and the second reader starts from there. So each reader reads from three verses: the first reads verses 1, 2 and half of 3, and the second reads the rest of verse 3 and verses 4 and 5.

keyTerms.meaning: Splits (divides a verse into two parts)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: He splits a verse.
phrases.notes: The middle verse is divided between the two readers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: An alternative answer to the same קשיא, disagreeing with רב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting verse 3 lets five verses cover two readers.

steps.title: Why doesn't רב allow splitting?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב chose repeating instead of the simpler idea of splitting a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב, who said 'he repeats', what is the reason he did not say 'he splits'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what bothered רב about שמואל's solution. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Splitting seems easy and avoids reading a verse twice. So רב must have a reason for rejecting it. The גמרא wants to know what that reason is.

phrases.english: And Rav, who said he repeats,
what is the reason he did not say he splits?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב דְּאָמַר דּוֹלֵג, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר פּוֹסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for רב's reasoning against שמואל's method.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רב rejects splitting a verse.

steps.title: רב: we don't divide a verse that משה didn't divide
steps.stepSummary: רב holds that a פסוק must stay as משה set it. We may not cut a verse that משה did not cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds: Any verse that משה did not divide, we do not divide.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב forbids splitting verses, so repeating a verse is the only option.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse divisions come from משה. Cutting a verse in half changes that structure. Reading a verse twice keeps every verse whole.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that we may not split a verse משה did not split, is the base for the challenge against שמואל in the next step.

phrases.english: He holds:
any verse that Moshe did not divide,
we do not divide it.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר: כׇּל פְּסוּקָא דְּלָא פַּסְקֵיהּ מֹשֶׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב forbids dividing a verse that משה did not divide.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: splitting was allowed only for schoolchildren
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל. רבי חנינא קרא reported that רבי חנינא הגדול let him split verses only when teaching young children.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said he splits, but may we split? Didn't רבי חנינא קרא say: I had great trouble with רבי חנינא הגדול, and he permitted me to split verses only for schoolchildren, since it is done so they can learn?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's view by bringing a source that limits splitting verses to teaching children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא קרא had to work hard to get any permission at all. Even then, he was allowed to split verses only for teaching schoolchildren. This suggests splitting is normally forbidden, which would rule out שמואל's answer for public Torah reading.

keyTerms.meaning: רבי חנינא the Bible expert, a teacher of מקרא
It is done for the purpose of learning

phrases.english: And Shmuel said he splits,
but may we split?
But didn't Rabbi Chanina the Bible expert say:
I had great trouble
with Rabbi Chanina the Great,
and he did not permit me to split verses
except for schoolchildren,
since it is done so that they can learn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from defending רב to challenging שמואל's view from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a verse is split in the reading of בראשית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Splitting verses was allowed only as a special exception for teaching children, so it should not be allowed in public Torah reading.

steps.title: שמואל: splitting is allowed when there is no other way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers on behalf of שמואל that the children's exception was based on necessity. Here too there is no other way, so splitting is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל: What is the reason there? Because it is not possible otherwise. Here too, it is not possible otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל's view. The real reason behind the schoolchildren case applies to the Torah reading too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The children's case was not a special rule only for teaching. The reason was that there was no other way to teach them. Two readers sharing five verses is also a case with no other way, so the same permission applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not possible (any other way)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways to split בראשית's five verses between two readers. רב: repeat a verse (דולג), because we never split a verse משה did not split. שמואל: split the middle verse (פוסק), because splitting is allowed when there is no other way.

phrases.english: And Shmuel would answer:
There, what is the reason?
Because it is not possible otherwise.
Here too, it is not possible otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 against שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the reason behind the source (necessity, not teaching children specifically)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Splitting verses was permitted only for teaching children.
steps.terutzMaskana: Splitting is permitted wherever there is no other option, including the reading of בראשית by two people.

steps.title: Why does שמואל reject repeating a verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now looks at שמואל's side and asks why he did not choose רב's approach of repeating a verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said that one splits the verse. What is his reason for not saying that one repeats a verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Earlier the גמרא asked why רב rejects splitting. Now it asks the same question in the other direction: why does שמואל reject repeating?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's reason was already given: we may not cut a פסוק that משה did not cut. Repeating a verse breaks no such rule, so we need to know what is wrong with it in שמואל's eyes. This question sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Splits a verse in half (שמואל's approach)
Literally 'skips back': repeats a verse already read (רב's approach)

phrases.english: And Shmuel said: he splits the verse.
phrases.notes: Restating שמואל's position so the גמרא can question it.

phrases.english: What is the reason he did not say: he repeats a verse?
phrases.notes: This mirrors the question asked about רב in step 22.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 22. Having explained רב's reasoning, the גמרא now asks for שמואל's reasoning.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What problem does שמואל see in repeating a verse that makes him prefer splitting?

steps.title: Repeating could mislead people who walk in or walk out
steps.stepSummary: Repeating a verse is forbidden by a rabbinic decree. People entering or leaving mid-reading might wrongly think a reader read fewer than three verses.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree because of those who come in, and a decree because of those who go out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that שמואל avoids repeating because it could confuse people who arrive late or leave early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the first reader reads verses 1-3, and the second reader repeats verse 3 and then reads verses 4 and 5. Someone who walks in during the second reading did not hear verse 3 the first time. He will think the first reader read only verses 1-2. Someone who leaves after the first reader will think only two verses were left for the second reader. Either person could conclude that it is fine to read fewer than three verses, so the חכמים made a גזירה against repeating.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to prevent a mistake
Those who come in (to the בית כנסת) during the reading
Those who leave during the reading

steps.confusionAlert: The worry is not that anyone actually reads too few verses. Everyone really reads three. The worry is only that onlookers will get the wrong impression and learn a wrong הלכה.

phrases.english: A decree because of those who enter
phrases.notes: A latecomer did not hear verse 3 read the first time. When the second reader repeats it, the latecomer thinks the first reader read only two verses.

phrases.english: and a decree because of those who leave.
phrases.notes: Someone who leaves after the first reader thinks only two verses are left for the second.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה מִשּׁוּם הַנִּכְנָסִין וּגְזֵרָה מִשּׁוּם הַיּוֹצְאִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Repeating a verse is forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה, because people entering or leaving could think a reader read fewer than three verses.
steps.whyThisMatters: Now both sides are explained. רב worries about cutting משה's verse. שמואל worries about how the reading looks to the public.

steps.title: A ברייתא about six-verse and five-verse sections
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. A five-verse פרשה is read by one person. If the first reader reads three, the second must continue into the next פרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: A section of six verses is read by two people, and a section of five is read by one. If the first person reads three, the second reads the last two of this section and one from the next section. Some say he reads three from the next section, because we do not start a section and read fewer than three of its verses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge both רב and שמואל. This step only quotes the source. The actual attack comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A six-verse section divides neatly into three plus three. A five-verse section cannot, so one person reads it. If two people did divide it, the ברייתא sends the second reader into the next section rather than repeating or splitting a verse. The יש אומרים require three verses from the new section, because one may not start a section and read fewer than three of its verses.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
A section or paragraph of the Torah

phrases.english: They raised an objection: A section of six verses
phrases.notes: מיתיבי signals that a challenge from a תנאי source is coming.

phrases.english: is read by two people,
phrases.notes: Three verses each.

phrases.english: and a section of five is read by one person.
phrases.notes: Five cannot be split into three and three.

phrases.english: And if the first person reads three,
phrases.notes: That is, they did divide a five-verse section.

phrases.english: the second reads two from this section
phrases.notes: The remaining verses 4 and 5.

phrases.english: and one from another section.
phrases.notes: He completes his three by moving forward, not by repeating or splitting.

phrases.english: And some say: three,
phrases.notes: He must read three verses from the next section.

phrases.english: because one does not begin a section
for fewer than three verses.
phrases.notes: Starting a new section requires reading at least three of its verses.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: With both positions explained, the גמרא now tests them against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא solves the five-verse problem by moving into the next section. It never mentions repeating or splitting. This suggests that neither method is used.

steps.title: Why doesn't the ברייתא repeat or split?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the attack openly. Each side should have used its own method in the ברייתא's case, yet the ברייתא uses neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the one who says 'repeat,' let him repeat! And according to the one who says 'split,' let him split!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the challenge from the ברייתא. Its case is just like ours, so why doesn't it use רב's repeating or שמואל's splitting?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, as in our case, two people are sharing a five-verse section. If רב is right, the second reader should simply repeat a verse. If שמואל is right, he should split a verse. The ברייתא instead sends him to the next section, which seems to contradict both.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the one who says

phrases.english: According to the one who says 'repeat,' let him repeat,
phrases.notes: Aimed at רב.

phrases.english: and according to the one who says 'split,' let him split!
phrases.notes: Aimed at שמואל.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר דּוֹלֵג לִידְלוֹג וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר פּוֹסֵק לִיפְסוֹק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ברייתא quoted in step 28 into a direct challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both רב's דולג and שמואל's פוסק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If either method were valid, the ברייתא would have used it. Since it goes to the next section instead, both methods seem rejected.

steps.title: The ברייתא's case is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to answer that the ברייתא's situation differs from ours. The explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its answer by saying the ברייתא's case is not like ours. This line only opens the answer. The actual difference comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שאני התם' tells us the ברייתא does not argue with רב or שמואל. It deals with a different situation, so a different solution was available there. We must wait for the next line to learn what makes it different.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there (a distinction is about to be drawn)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the ברייתא disproves רב and שמואל. The גמרא is about to explain why that case can be solved differently.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: Opening formula of a distinction. The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge of step 29.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to reject both repeating and splitting.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא's case is different from ours. The specific difference is given in the continuation.
